newsitem.title: USA: Brooke to hike prices for tobacco deal costs.
newsitem.headline: Brooke to hike prices for tobacco deal costs.

text.p: Bennett LeBow, chairman of Brooke Group Ltd said Thursday that the company's Liggett Group would raise prices of cigarettes if legislation is enacted to carry out a tobacco settlement.
In a letter to state attorneys general, LeBow criticized comments made by Richard Scruggs, a key negotiator in tobacco settlements, that were published in the Wall Street Journal and Washington Post.
Scruggs' comments were in response to a letter LeBow sent to the legal officers on Wednesday denouncing last week's $368.5 billion settlement.
In Thursday's letter, LeBow took issue with Scruggs' statements that LeBow was getting "far more than he bargained for" in the deal.
The Washington Post said that Scruggs noted that Liggett had been exempted from paying its share of the up front multi-billion dollar industry payment.

"Allowing Liggett to escape the annual payout, Scruggs said would have allowed Liggett to charge much less per pack, making its brands more attractive to younger smokers," the Washington Post reported.
He said the amount Liggett would "save" is negligible, because the upfront payment is based solely on market capitalization not market share.
He said the binding agreement with Liggett provides that the company is not obliged to make an upfront payment.

"Likewise, Mr. Scruggs' statement that Liggett would have a price advantage is just not true. We made it clear to you, and we restate it now, that if legislation is enacted Liggett will raise the prices of its cigarettes in step with the other companies so long as the payment terms of our March 1997 agreement are honored."
